household.name: Black and white shoulder bag with image of a horse
household.title: Black and white shoulder bag with image of a horse
household.reason: This is a wool morral shoulder bag with a knitted horse motif, a men's carrying bag documented as made and worn by Maya men in Guatemala, matching the claimed culture and its everyday craft tradition.

household.name: bikupa
household.title: bikupa
household.reason: The image shows a hollowed log beehive (bikupa) used by Yucatan Maya beekeepers for traditional stingless bee apiculture, matching the claimed ethnicity and use.

household.name: behållare, ämbar, spann
household.title: behållare, ämbar, spann
household.reason: The image shows a folded bark-bag vessel (choy) with a reinforcing ring and carrying cord, collected in Xcacal, Quintana Roo, a documented Yucatec Maya settlement, matching the claimed Maya household object.

household.name: hängmatta, Hamaca
household.title: hängmatta, Hamaca
household.reason: The image shows a woven maguey-fiber hammock from Yucatán, Mexico, purchased at a Mexican folk-art museum and attributed to the Maya, a household textile item consistent with traditional Maya craft.

household.name: Schoudertas met quetzalmotief
household.title: Schoudertas met quetzalmotief
household.reason: A handmade crocheted wool shoulder bag (morral) with quetzal bird motifs, from Nahualá, Sololá, a Maya (K'iche') town in Guatemala known for this male bag style — a genuine Maya-made everyday object.

household.name: Shoulder bag
household.title: Shoulder bag
household.reason: The image shows a crocheted maguey-fiber shoulder bag with colored stripes, a traditional men's accessory from Todos Santos, a Maya (Mam) town in Guatemala — consistent with Maya material culture.

garment.name: Roze ceintuur met geometrische motieven
garment.title: Roze ceintuur met geometrische motieven
garment.reason: The image shows a pink woven belt (faja) with geometric and figurative embroidery and fringed ends, a backstrap-woven garment worn by Maya women in Guatemala to secure a wrap skirt, consistent with the claimed ethnicity and category.

garment.name: Gestreepte hemd
garment.title: Gestreepte hemd
garment.reason: A striped cotton man's shirt (hemd) with brocaded collar and cuffs, backstrap-loom woven, from Nahualá, Sololá — a well-known Maya (K'iche') men's garment type from Guatemala's highlands. This matches Maya traditional dress.

garment.name: Children's hat with motifs of animals
garment.title: Children's hat with motifs of animals
garment.reason: The image shows a black backstrap-loomed textile with colorful brocaded animal and floral motifs, identified as a Maya child's montera (headcloth) from Chuarrancho, Guatemala — a traditional Maya woven garment type.

garment.name: Red headband
garment.title: Red headband
garment.reason: A red woven wool hairband from Colotenango, Huehuetenango, worn daily by Mam women — the Mam are a Maya people, so this traditional handwoven garment fits the claimed Maya ethnicity.

garment.name: Yellow wrapskirt with jasmine
garment.title: Yellow wrapskirt with jasmine
garment.reason: This is a yellow wraparound skirt (corte) with woven plaid striping, matching the museum's description of Maya women's traditional wraparound skirts of ancient origin. It is a clear, whole example of Maya garment weaving.

garment.name: blus, huipil
garment.title: blus, huipil
garment.reason: The image shows a huipil blouse with woven red/pink stripes and an embroidered floral neckline, a classic Maya women's garment purchased at markets in Guatemala; general regional attribution to Maya is reasonable even without a specific local identification.

garment.name: Ceintuur met slangmotief
garment.title: Ceintuur met slangmotief
garment.reason: A backstrap-loom woven belt (ceintuur) with brocaded geometric motifs in dark blue striped ground and vivid pink/multicolor patterned panels, a garment type worn by Maya women in Guatemala to secure their wrapped skirts, consistent with the claimed ethnicity.

garment.name: Red women's shirt
garment.title: Red women's shirt
garment.reason: This is a hand-woven backstrap-loom shirt with brocaded multicolored motifs on striped cotton, a garment type made and worn by Maya women in Guatemala for daily use.

garment.name: Feesthoed met veren en een stukje spiegel
garment.title: Feesthoed met veren en een stukje spiegel
garment.reason: This is a feathered festival headdress worn for the "Baile de la Conquista" dance performed by K'iche' Maya communities in Totonicapán, Guatemala, matching the claimed ethnicity and made with embroidered velvet, mirror-glass and feathers typical of this dance costume.

garment.name: Ceintuur met zigzaglijnen
garment.title: Ceintuur met zigzaglijnen
garment.reason: This is a woven faja (belt/sash) with brocaded zigzag patterns and fringe, a traditional garment worn by Maya women in Guatemala to secure their wrapped skirt, matching the description exactly.

textile.name: Red cloth with bird motives
textile.title: Red cloth with bird motives
textile.reason: A red cotton backstrap-loom woven cloth (tzute) with rows of embroidered bird/animal motifs in purple, matching Maya textile tradition of Guatemala as described.

textile.name: Rode doek met geometrische motieven
textile.title: Rode doek met geometrische motieven
textile.reason: A red backstrap-loom woven servilleta cloth with embroidered bands of birds and maize cobs, the characteristic red identified with the Ixil Maya villages (Cotzal, Nebaj, Chajul) — a textile made and used by this people.

textile.name: Cloth with images of birds
textile.title: Cloth with images of birds
textile.reason: A dark cotton tzute-type cloth with rows of colorful woven bird motifs and fringed ends, matching the Maya textile tradition of Guatemala described in the museum notes.

textile.name: Cloth with bird motifs
textile.title: Cloth with bird motifs
textile.reason: A striped cotton tzute/sut with colorful brocaded bird motifs and fringed ends, a garment type made and used by Maya highland weavers in Guatemala for carrying, ceremonial, or head-covering purposes, matching the claimed ethnicity well.

textile.name: Cloth with double-headed eagles
textile.title: Cloth with double-headed eagles
textile.reason: This is a brocaded Guatemalan tzute/sut with dense polychrome geometric and figural motifs (including double-headed eagle designs), a classic Maya-made multipurpose cloth used for head covering, carrying, or ceremonial purposes.

textile.name: Draagdoek in Mexicaanse stijl
textile.title: Draagdoek in Mexicaanse stijl
textile.reason: A backstrap-loom-woven, brightly striped carrying cloth (tzute/perraje-type textile) of the kind made and used by Maya women in Guatemala (the record even names Nahualá, a K'iche' Maya town), consistent with claimed Maya attribution despite the odd Dutch title "Mexican style."

masks-ritual.name: mask
masks-ritual.title: mask
masks-ritual.reason: A carved wooden demon/animal mask with fangs and horn-like ears, collected in Cobán, Alta Verapaz, Guatemala — a Maya (Q'eqchi') region known for ritual dance masks used in traditional fiestas. This is a plausible traditional Maya ritual object.

sculpture.name: figurine
sculpture.title: figurine
sculpture.reason: A pottery figurine of a crocodile with textured, bumpy skin, attributed by the museum to Maya makers; crocodile/caiman effigy figures are a well-known part of Mesoamerican Maya ceramic traditions.
